newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares at new record high in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares at new record high in brisk trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hit another record high on Thursday, rising 0.89 percent in active trading, the Capital Market Authority (CMA)said in a report.
The CMA's all-share index closed at 415.18 points, its 18th highest level in as many trading days on turnover of 122.46 million pounds ($36.02 million).
"It is not unusually high turnover these days, with more increases expected,"broker Mohamed Magdi of Hermes/EFG told Reuters.
Trading in the market targeted many sectors, with the chemicals, cement and banking sectors appearing on the most actively traded list, brokers said.
"The market is not yet overvalued and more rises are expected,"Hany el-Sayyed of El-Rashad Brokerage said.
"We are still in the boom because of the high liquidity, coming from foreign investors," he added.
Magdi also said the recent increases had been unexpected in the fasting month of Ramadan, when activity is normally slow, but added that "a growth of 15 percent is yet expected before a correction."
Helwan Portland Cement was the day's most active stock, with shares worth 67.68 million pounds changing hands. But the share ended down 0.26 pounds at 80.25.
Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries came second on the top ten list in terms of volume. The share rose 5.14 pounds to close at 108.04, after shares worth 61.32 million pounds were traded.

Brokers said the banking sector had become popular with foreign investors who have been actively buying shares during the past few days. Misr International Bank/MIBANK lept another 33.68 to 707.30 pounds in trade worth 55.81 million pounds.
The bank has proposed tranfering some shares through a global depository receipt offering and that continued to spur trade, brokers said.
Among other active shares were North Cairo Flour Mills, which ended down 8.00 to 192.00 and Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals which closed 2.20 higher at 147.00 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 700.83 points from 687.29 on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 271.35 from 270.96 points.
Out of the 84 shares traded, 42 gained, 23 lost and 19 ended the day unchanged.
